summary: Implemented the PH-349 PostgreSQL multi-connection concurrency acceptance slice at BASE a5ba2fd. tests/test_v1_pg_concurrency.py contains (a) a CLI/probe runner aligned with PH-345: --dsn/PMO_PG_DSN/DATABASE_URL resolution, JSON evidence envelope (script/contract_version/mode/profile/app_sha/started_at/finished_at/exit_code/status/checks/artifacts/redactions/notes), frozen exit-code mapping (0 pass, 2 not_run/prerequisite, 3 assertion fail, 4 environment fail, 5 security reject), and (b) real PostgreSQL probes that create a random isolated schema and drop it: company advisory-lock serialization (V1-OPS-06.1), concurrent unique receipt for the same org+request_token (06.2), append-only trigger rejection of UPDATE/DELETE (06.3), opposite-order locking deadlock detection plus rollback retry success (06.4). SQLite or non-PostgreSQL DSNs are rejected with exit 2 and never treated as concurrency evidence; missing DSN yields not_run; unreachable PG yields exit 4. The module also provides always-runnable contract tests (envelope shape/status mapping, missing/SQLite/non-PG DSN rejection, CLI exit 2 envelopes, unreachable PG exit 4) and a PG probe test class that skips with an explicit not_run reason when no real DSN is configured. docs/engineering/pg-concurrency.md documents invocation, probe matrix, envelope, exit codes, isolation/redaction rules, business-level PG suites and the honest current not_run status. No production data was touched; no business tables, migrations, code paths or contracts were changed.

deviations: Real PostgreSQL was not available locally, so the PG probe test is skipped with an explicit not_run reason; the slice delivers the executable probe/CLI and contract tests, not a local PG pass. Real PG evidence is delegated to CI/deployment and must not be replaced by SQLite.

No scripts/ops/* file was created because the BASE PH-349 allowed_paths only include tests/test_v1_pg_concurrency.py/docs; the executable runner is therefore the test module CLI (`python -m tests.test_v1_pg_concurrency --dsn ...`), which produces the same PH-345 envelope and exit codes.
The probe file uses psycopg3 (the installed PostgreSQL driver) directly with random throwaway schemas and no business tables; it does not modify applied migrations or production data.

Business-level concurrency (double approval, over-clearance, refunds, allocation, opening balances, close, invoice reversal, FX snapshots) is covered by existing owner concurrency suites on PG; this slice adds infrastructure probes (lock/idempotency/append-only/deadlock) and documents the business-set linkage rather than duplicating those suites.

Full-suite first run showed a transient delivery_execution heartbeat failure; it passed in isolation and in the rerun, and the stable full-run failure set equals the clean main baseline (5F+3E), so it is recorded as pre-existing flakiness, not a new regression.
